# Spec: Adaptive review

**Generated by:** li-plan on 2026-09-28
**Status:** APPROVED - current user authority; independent spec and quality re-review passed
**Design and tasks:** [plan.md](plan.md)
**Decision:** [ADR-0040](../../decisions/0040-adaptive-review.md)

## Architecture overview

Improve the existing Review Method, not a second scanner, policy engine or release
gate. A small deterministic helper translates evidenced consequence facts into
lean, standard or deep review. Existing question selection, packet rendering and
single/MARS assessment consume that result. Explicit mandatory questions and
advisory exploration remain distinct. ADR-0028 owns release evidence; ADR-0029 owns
profile resolution; ADR-0036 owns MARS consent, model identity and adjudication.

An optional, lazy pattern adapter calls the reusable-patterns provider's existing
parse/verify/project/review functions from the trusted installed source. That
provider is not yet on main. Missing capability is unavailable, not an empty
catalog. No pack-schema or resolver change belongs to this initiative.

Offline evaluation measures imported review observations and, separately, imported
benchmark results. It runs no model, network request, target, exploit, container or
submission. No fixture result is evidence of model quality or leaderboard rank.

## Data model / interfaces / contracts

### Evidenced depth

`lib/review_context.py` owns `assess_depth(context, requested="auto")`. Context is
schema-version 1 with `facts` and `evidence` mappings and
`asserted_by: {actor, reference}` identifying the declared source of the assessment.
Known facts require nonblank evidence references. The six axes are:

| Fact | Values |
|---|---|
| deployment | local, internal, production, unknown |
| exposure | isolated, trusted, untrusted, unknown |
| impact | reversible, sensitive, irreversible, unknown |
| behavior_change | true, false, unknown |
| security_boundary | true, false, unknown |
| blast_radius | contained, shared, unknown |

Deep is the floor for production, untrusted exposure, sensitive/irreversible
impact, a changed security boundary or shared blast radius. Lean is available
only when every fact is known, no behavior/security-boundary change is present,
the impact is reversible and the scope is contained/local-or-internal.
Other known cases use standard. Unknown facts produce at least standard with
`status: needs-context`; they are never evidence of a low-risk change.
An explicit lower depth is refused; a higher depth is allowed. Depth never
selects a model, consents to MARS or authorizes execution.

The result identifies requested/minimum/selected depth, reasons, unknown facts,
source evidence, applicable extra question tags and recommended independence.
It always has `release_clearance: false`. No-context rendering is standard and
`needs-context`, never lean. Standard keeps existing subject/tag selection.
Lean keeps all universal and applicable questions but adds no depth-only lenses;
it is not permission to skip substantive independent review. Deep additionally
selects `deep-review`; production adds `production`. Untrusted exposure,
sensitive/irreversible impact or a changed security boundary adds
`security-critical`. Unknown facts add `risk-unknown` at every depth, including standard.

Facts are declared observations, not authenticated truths. Keep the asserting
actor/reference with their packet context; bind the fact file and its evidence
in the existing selection. A reviewer can contest them with a finding against
the ordinary contract/trust-boundary question; stop the affected result and
reassess instead of silently keeping a lean classification.

### Existing method extension

Question catalogs retain schema 1 and stable IDs. An optional
`requirement: mandatory|advisory` defaults to advisory in both base and extension
catalogs. The shipped base questions remain advisory exploration; explicit
selected acceptance/controls or an approved catalog declare mandatory questions.
Catalog approval comes from the actual project/policy owner and its accepted
source revision in the existing review selection, not a self-asserted JSON flag.
Depth never changes a question's requirement. Selected mandatory IDs are included
in method metadata and the immutable packet. Explicit additional required IDs
must be selected and active, never silently dropped; superseded or out-of-selection
required IDs are errors.
Missing question rows remain incomplete. An explained advisory `not-checked`
remains a visible limitation; a mandatory `not-checked` is incomplete.
Grounded question N/A remains possible, but cannot override an applicable
mandatory acceptance/control. The pattern provider alone classifies effective
mandatory/default/waived clauses; this adapter never reinterprets a `must` string.

Single reports and MARS round-one reports call the same assessment function with
the same mandatory inventory. New method metadata is version 2 and requires
that inventory; absence is an error, not legacy fallback. Keep header syntax v1.
Check new metadata against the original packet body, including its hash and
selected/required inventory, before accepting a report; the packet CLI accepts
a new explicit `--body` for this purpose. MARS attaches the complete inventory after
checking its frozen brief. Legacy v1 metadata remains readable as legacy evidence,
not a way to claim newly required coverage. The body, rather than a parallel
panel prompt, carries depth, selected questions, source references and pattern
context. This is consistency checking, not authentication; ADR-0028 still binds
the caller's accepted obligations and result.

### Optional pattern adapter

The adapter consumes explicit roots, lock, actual work context, companion task
map, original package ID and optional coverage files. It imports only the trusted
sibling `lib/patterns.py`, calls that provider's parsers and `verify_lock` before
`project_package`, and calls `review_coverage` when actual coverage is supplied.
It preserves complete mandatory clauses, returned settings, exceptions and
original task IDs. Asset references are metadata only; no automatic reads or
network fetches. The normal pattern `read_asset` route remains responsible for
an explicitly needed selected document.

This is only a context adapter. The provider's `review_coverage` / `li-pattern review`
result remains the supplemental ADR-0028 control; clause IDs never become
standing-question IDs or a second release gate. Provider failures/statuses remain
visible. Pattern-unavailable does not prevent unrelated review with no known
pattern/policy dependency, but it remains unavailable. Only a current successful
launcher list/resolve result bound into the selection establishes no applicable
patterns. A missing lock/helper/directory never establishes that outcome.
The adapter does not manufacture roots, parse pack YAML, infer an empty catalog
from file absence, re-resolve defaults, rebind profiles or write locks.
The calling workflow must obtain a current envelope through the existing
ADR-0029/pattern launcher and include its inputs in the content-bound selection.

### Offline evaluation

Use standard-library JSON only and explicit input paths. A fixed nonempty case
inventory and run identity prevent success-only denominator selection. Review
metrics distinguish accepted findings, false positives, missed findings,
incomplete/error cases and supplied latency/token measurements. Comparisons
require matching task/model/tool/environment/budget identities. Zero denominators
produce an explicit unavailable metric, never perfect quality.

Benchmark receipts are a separate mode. Preserve benchmark/source and verifier
revision, dataset revision, level/split, planned tasks, attempts and supplied
verification-result provenance. For CyberGym the primary metric uses exactly one
operator-designated final submission per task, never the best available attempt.
Compute it only from supplied upstream exit records: vulnerable exit nonzero and
not timeout 300, fixed exit zero. Missing/unverifiable/undesignated records do not
count as successes. Reject contradictory supplied success flags. Any-of-attempts
is a separately labeled diagnostic, not the headline metric.

Reject duplicate/unknown identities, contradictory outcomes and malformed metrics.
Unrun/error results remain in the planned denominator. Include task-set and input
hashes, actual subset size and a Wilson 95% interval; do not invent a sample-size
threshold or infer representativeness. Refuse matched comparisons across different
level, metric, task set, attempt budget, model/tools, network/dynamic-environment or
cross-task-memory settings. Label results imported observations, not independently
verified benchmark runs or public leaderboard scores.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Source | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Consequence-based depth, evidence for known facts, no silent downgrade | Current request; ADR-0026/0028 | T1, T2, T7 |
| R2 | Cheap path has no network/model/panel work; deep does not grant authority | Current request; ADR-0036 | T1, T2, T7, T10 |
| R3 | Tough, source-attributed security and correctness questions selected only when relevant | Current request; existing Review Method | T8, T10 |
| R4 | Mandatory unknown evidence cannot pass; optional limitations and grounded N/A remain distinct | ADR-0028; current request | T7, T9 |
| R5 | Single and MARS share exact packet and assessment semantics | ADR-0036 | T7, T9 |
| R6 | Established repository/pack patterns and selected internal assets use the existing provider | Current request; patterns ADR-0038 direction | T3, T4, T10, T11 |
| R7 | No conflicting parser, pack schema, native generator, profile or release ledger | Concurrent-owner handoffs | T3, T7, T10, T11 |
| R8 | Honest offline review/benchmark measurement, no offensive execution or rank claims | Current request; ADR-0021 | T5, T6, T12 |
| R9 | On-demand references remain under 20 KB; native body changes are bounded | Verified size-owner handoff | T10, T11 |
| R10 | Question calibration proposes human-reviewed changes; never removes rare severe checks automatically | Current request; existing outcome log | T8, T10 |
| R11 | Hermetic negative/positive tests and independent exact-tree review | Repository protocol | T2, T4, T6, T9, T11, T12 |
| R12 | Additive, attributable integration with frozen patterns and native-parity ownership | Current request | T11, T12 |

## Constraints and exclusions

- No edits to the parallel initiatives' frozen artifacts, the shared todo.md,
  native generators/adapters/hooks, cli_support frontmatter, or their reserved
  plugin version. ADR-0038 and ADR-0039 are reserved; this work reserves ADR-0040.
- Do not reopen the separate review-remediation hold. In particular, no unrelated
  trusted-source fallback, hook registration, neutrality, header-deduplication,
  performance or publication-guard repair.
- Preserve selected task/acceptance authority, profile drift checks, latest
  rejection, dirty/new/deleted content binding and real review independence.
- No external private policy acquisition, credentials, live changes, benchmark
  execution, exploits, target probing, automatic submissions or model superiority
  claims. Learn public engineering ideas with attribution, not proprietary text.
- Do not change MARS defaults or infer that this Opus worker request authorizes
  arbitrary future panels. Workers request Opus 5.5, high, long_context; actual
  context capacity is not known from that request alone.

## Open integration boundaries

Reusable patterns is frozen at `64338b6c9fc30fb3618cc9f46b66d8b0d2ab1e7c`
(product `fdb9f27b`) and is not release-cleared or on main. Test an isolated join
without mutating that branch. Native-client parity owns full-body generation and
version 0.13.0; refresh its generated output only after its accepted integration,
not by hand. Publication identity is unresolved; no credentials may be inspected
or switched to manufacture a push.
